angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 466,119 km at 64.40 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.5277 +/- 0.0260 mas (same row, RUWE 1.54): 64.40 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.67 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar radius of WASP-107 b's parameter set from Howard et al. 2025 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract): 466,119 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.683 +/- 0.017 solar masses from Piaulet et al. 2021, the stellar mass of WASP-107 b's parameter set from Piaulet et al. 2021 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161...70P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4425 +/- 70 K from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of WASP-107 b's parameter set from Howard et al. 2025 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of WASP-107 b's parameter set from Howard et al. 2025 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-107.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.620, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-107 (pscomppars): spectral type K6, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-107 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.02 dex, from Howard et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-107 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.87943, from Piaulet et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161...70P/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-107 (pscomppars): age 3.4 Gyr, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-107 (pscomppars): rotation period 17.1 d, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-107 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.507 km/s, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.67 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.257. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
